title: Compatibility lint for fallback variant toolchains
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Create an automated compatibility linter and CI gating workflow to detect and prevent tokenizer, context, KV-cache, and tooling parity regressions across fallback model variants used by smart routing (region/tier routing and variant fallback paths). This ticket covers design, implementation, and rollout of the lint rules, baseline corpora for checks, CI integration, and dashboarding for violations.

Goals:
- Prevent runtime mismatches that cause silent degradation when smart routing falls back between variants (e.g., different tokenization, unexpected special tokens, KV cache layout differences).
- Provide actionable diagnostics and auto-fix suggestions where safe (e.g., tokenizer normalization, canonical special token mapping).
- Gate PRs that change variant toolchains/materialization with clear failure messages.

Success criteria (measurable):
- CI lint runs produce zero new failures for 95% of variant change PRs within first 2 weeks of rollout.
- Post-deployment incidents caused by tokenizer/KV incompatibilities drop by 80% for fallback events in next quarter.
- Linter identifies at least 90% of seeded parity issues from our synthetic test corpus.

Scope:
In-scope: tokenizer token boundary/offset mapping checks, special-token canonicalization, sequence-length/context-window consistency checks, KV cache header/layout signature checks, streaming API semantics parity (e.g., event ordering and partial tokenization), tooling/runtime flags that affect inference output (quantization runtime differences that change output tokenization behavior).
Out-of-scope: model architecture semantic divergences (intent/behavior), guardrails on content moderation parity (handled by separate evals).

Approach / Implementation plan:
1) Rule design: Enumerate parity checks and their strictness levels (error vs warn vs suggest). Rules will include: tokenization map equivalence, tokenizer ID/metadata match, canonical special token mapping, max_context and sliding-window behavior check, KV header checksum/signature, cached-kv shape compatibility, streaming chunk boundary expectations.
2) Baseline corpora: Build small canonical prompt set composed of edge cases (Unicode mixes, long-context, streaming partial tokens, role-content delimiting tokens) and a seeded mutation set for regression testing.
3) Linter prototype: Implement a Rust CLI tool (fast, portable) that runs offline and in CI; provide a Python wrapper for local dev DX. The tool will run paired comparisons between a candidate variant toolchain and a golden reference.
4) CI integration: Add a lightweight job to variant onboarding and variant-change PRs. Fail on critical parity errors. Include an allowlist mechanism for known, documented intentional deviations.
5) Telemetry & Dashboard: Emit structured lint results to the Console under the new "variant-parity-lint" trace to enable triage and historical tracking.
6) Rollout: Canary the gating to one routing tier (dev-tier) for 1 week, then expand to staging, then prod tiers. Provide a feature-flagged bypass for emergency ops with audit logs.

Trade-offs & notes:
- Strict equal-tokenization enforcement can block legitimate optimizations (e.g., safe tokenizer normalization across quantized runtimes). We'll provide a graded rule set and opt-in auto-fix where safe.
- Running full model tokenization in CI is expensive; we will use lightweight tokenizers for fast checks and a nightly full-variant exercise that runs heavier instrumentation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Linter binary + Python wrapper in repo with unit tests and example golden comparisons.
- CI job in variant-change pipeline with failing status on critical errors and documented bypass process.
- Confluence doc describing rules, allowlist process, and escalation path.
- Dashboard card showing lint pass rate by variant and routing tier.
